newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ICAC says arrests six HK Standard staff.
newsitem.headline: ICAC says arrests six HK Standard staff.

text.p: Hong Kong's graft watchdog, the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC), said on Wednesday it had arrested four employees of Hong Kong Standard Newspapers Ltd and two former staff members.
In a statement, the ICAC said it had arrested three serving and one former senior official, and one former and one serving circulation supervisor of Hong Kong Standard Newspapers Ltd.
The company publishes the English-language Hong Kong Standard and Sunday Standard newspapers.
The ICAC said it had "revealed a scheme which involved the deliberate excess printing of over 10,000 extra copies of the newspapers each day, which were purported sold to a bogus bulk distributor".
The surplus was actually sold as waste paper, the ICAC said.

"ICAC inquiries have disclosed that since at least early 1994, the circulation figures of the Hong Kong Standard and Sunday Standard newspapers have been fraudulently and systematically inflated to deceive a U.K.-based circulation audit company and local advertising clients of both newspapers," the graft watchdog said.
"ICAC inquiries also indicated that more recently the deliberately printed surplus and systematic disposal has ranged from 14,000 up to 23,000 copies per day."
The newspapers' editorial operations were not subject of the investigation, the ICAC said, with the inquiries limited to the printing, circulation, sales and marketing activities.
The ICAC said it had executed search warrants at the company's office and at the homes of some current and former staff.
